Ziekenhuis Gelderse Vallei (Ede)
Department of Radiology
Date: 03 Feb 2025
Exam: mpMRI prostate

Clinical indication: Re-evaluation of prostate cancer. PSA 6.4 ng/mL. Prior biopsy Gleason 3+5.

FINDINGS:
Prostate volume is 41.62 mL. T2-weighted imaging demonstrates a focal lesion in the peripheral zone, left base, measuring approximately 12 mm. The lesion shows restricted diffusion on DWI with corresponding signal drop on the ADC map. Dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) imaging demonstrates early, focal enhancement within the same region. No evidence of extracapsular extension or seminal vesicle invasion is seen. No suspicious lymph nodes or bone lesions are identified.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS v2.1 category 4 lesion in the left peripheral zone base.
Prostate-specific antigen density (PSAD): 0.154 ng/mL/mL.
Clinical T stage: cT1c.
csPCa predicted probability 0.80504376.

previous_notes.author: Dr. P. van Dijk (GP)
previous_notes.text: Patient presented with an elevated PSA of 5.1 ng/mL. Digital rectal examination was unremarkable. A transrectal ultrasound-guided biopsy was performed. The pathology report returned showing Gleason 3+5 (ISUP GG4) in the transition zone. The patient was referred to urology for further management discussion.

pathology_report:
Biopsy 1 (08 Jun 2024): Histological examination of the prostate tissue reveals adenocarcinoma. The Gleason score is 3+5, corresponding to ISUP grade group 4. The predominant growth pattern is acinar. No cribriform or intraductal patterns identified. The tumour is located in the transition zone, base.

Summary: The patient has undergone one biopsy to date, which demonstrated ISUP grade group 4 disease. The histological trajectory remains at this grade group.

AI-predicted ISUP grade group (digital pathology): grade group 3.
